description: GNU Bison is a general-purpose parser generator.
It converts an annotated context-free grammar into a deterministic LR or generalized LR (GLR) parser.

option.name: --color
tip: Whether to colorize the diagnostics.
Possible values: always, yes, never, no, auto, tty.
The value must be attached with =.

option.name: --debug
tip: Instrument the parser for tracing.
Same as -Dparse.trace.

option.name: --define
tip: Similar to '%define NAME VALUE'.
The delimiters are part of VALUE.

option.name: --defines
tip: Also produce a header file.
The file name is optional.

option.name: --feature
tip: Activate miscellaneous features.
Possible values: caret, diagnostics-show-caret, fixit, diagnostics-parseable-fixits, syntax-only, all, none.
The value must be attached: -f<FEATURES> or --feature=<FEATURES>.

option.name: --file-prefix
tip: Specify a prefix for output files.

option.name: --file-prefix-map
tip: Replace prefix OLD with NEW when writing file paths in output files.

option.name: --fixed-output-files
tip: Imitate Yacc's output file naming conventions (deprecated, use -o y.tab.c instead).

option.name: --force-define
tip: Like --define, but overrides a '%define NAME VALUE' from the grammar.

option.name: --graph
tip: Also output a graph of the automaton.
The file name is optional.

option.name: --help
tip: Display this help and exit.

option.name: --html
tip: Also output an HTML report of the automaton.
The file name is optional.

option.name: --language
tip: Specify the output programming language.
Currently supported languages include C, C++, D and Java.
Possible values: c, c++, d, java.

option.name: --locations
tip: Enable location support.

option.name: --name-prefix
tip: Prepend PREFIX to the external symbols.
(deprecated by -Dapi.prefix={PREFIX})

option.name: --no-lines
tip: Don't generate '#line' directives.

option.name: --output
tip: Leave output to FILE.

option.name: --print-datadir
tip: Output the directory containing skeletons and XSLT and exit.

option.name: --print-localedir
tip: Output the directory containing locale-dependent data and exit.

option.name: --report
tip: Also produce details on the automaton.
Possible values: states, itemsets, lookaheads, solved, counterexamples, cex, all, none.

option.name: --report-file
tip: Write the report to FILE.

option.name: --skeleton
tip: Specify the skeleton to use.
A name without '/' is resolved in the Bison installation directory.

option.name: --style
tip: Specify the CSS file for colorized diagnostics.

option.name: --token-table
tip: Include a table of token names.

option.name: --trace
tip: Report internal Bison traces (for debugging).
Possible values: none, locations, scan, parse, automaton, bitsets, closure, grammar, resource, all.
The value must be attached: -T<TRACES> or --trace=<TRACES>.

option.name: --update
tip: Apply fixes to the source grammar file and exit.

option.name: --verbose
tip: Same as '--report=state'.

option.name: --version
tip: Output version information and exit.

option.name: --warnings
tip: Report the warnings falling in CATEGORY.
Possible values: conflicts-sr, conflicts-rr, counterexamples, cex, dangling-alias, deprecated, empty-rule, midrule-values, precedence, yacc, other, all, none, everything, error.
Turn a category off by prefixing it with 'no-'.
Use 'error=CATEGORY' to treat that category as an error.
The value must be attached: -W<CATEGORY> or --warnings=<CATEGORY>.

option.name: --xml
tip: Also output an XML report of the automaton.
The file name is optional.

option.name: --yacc
tip: Emulate POSIX Yacc.
Imitate Yacc's diagnostics and output file naming conventions.

option.name: -d
tip: Also produce a header file, but cannot specify FILE (for POSIX Yacc).
